commander: Major General Alvan C. Gillem Jr.
current_activity: takes over the 17-mile Ninth Army front west of Geilenkirchen as its first operational sector
notes: Event date: 8 November 1944 (Siegfried p401: "Controlling the 113th Cavalry Group and the complete 102d Division, General Gillem's XIII Corps on 8 November took over defense of the seventeen-mile line west of Geilenkirchen"; p399: the corps had recently arrived from a Normandy staging area with no troops; the 4 November Ninth Army directive had given it the defensive line). Event definition: activation here means the corps' first operational sector: XIII Corps takes over a front with its first troops (the 113th Cavalry Group and the complete 102nd Division); the headquarters itself existed earlier (it had recently arrived from a Normandy staging area, p399) and Ninth Army had it assigned from 4 November; the British XXX Corps began arriving the next day to relieve it. Relationship: Ninth Army assigned (Siegfried p399, p401; CMH tables for the 84th and 102nd Divisions list XIII Corps from 7-8 November). Location: The atlas lists Tongeren from 26 October, 13 days earlier; no later place in the window before 8 November. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Tongeren. Event support: high (Green Book narrative). Location support: low (13 days to the nearest atlas entry; the headquarters is not tied to the date).

commander: Major General Alvan C. Gillem Jr.
current_activity: begins its push to the Roer: takes six miles of front from the Wurm at Müllendorf to the XIX Corps boundary below Ederen
notes: Event date: 24 November 1944 (Siegfried p565: not until the day after the XIX Corps reached the Roer did the XIII Corps commence the push to the river; by nightfall of 24 November Gillem had assumed responsibility for about six miles of front from the Wurm at Muellendorf to the new boundary with the XIX Corps below Ederen; p543: the arrival of the XIII Corps and the adjustment of the corps boundary on 24 November). Event definition: the XIII Corps, relieved of its holding line by the British, takes its own offensive sector on the left of the XIX Corps; the row is the sector takeover, not a headquarters move. Relationship: Ninth Army assigned. Location: The atlas lists Tongeren from 26 October only; the corps was then further east (Geilenkirchen area); the place is the last listed headquarters and is not tied to the date. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Tongeren. Event support: high (two Green Book pages). Location support: low (a 29-day gap to the nearest atlas entry).

current_activity: corps headquarters at Klötze as the corps takes over the triangle between the Aller and the Elbe
notes: Event date: 17 April 1945 (ww2byday, XIII Corps map unit: headquarters at Klötze on 17 April 1945; Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 400: a regiment of the 29th Division cleared the Klötze Forest, and the German forays delayed for a day a start on the new assignment handed the XIII Corps to assume responsibility for the vast triangle of unoccupied territory north of the Harz). Event definition: the corps headquarters is at Klötze on the date; the Green Book gives the new assignment of the corps in the same passage. Relationship: Ninth Army assigned (CR0191, standing relation). Location: Kloetze (ww2byday, XIII Corps map unit R476: the command post listed on 17 April 1945; the page compiles the CMH ETO order of battle); the town centre stands for the headquarters. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Klötze. Event support: moderate (one atlas listing and one Green Book passage). Location support: moderate (named town, listed on the date; one secondary compilation of an official list, no second source for the place).
